predictedBugs: Removing sheetRows could make SheetJS traverse an attacker-controlled inflated !ref before blank-row filtering; both runtimes now compact the range from material cells before sheet_to_json.
Counting formatted empty cells as populated could reject a 144-contact workbook with a styled tail; empty raw and formatted values are excluded while formulas are still rejected first.
Removing the row cap could accidentally remove every workload bound; byte, populated-cell, column, cell-length, sheet-count, timeout and worker-memory limits remain enforced.
A 10 MB highly compressed XLSX could expand before populated-cell validation; central-directory expansion, ratio, entry and path bounds now run before SheetJS.
A configured signed-out caller could consume worker resources during preview; workspace authority now resolves and fails closed before base64 decoding or parsing.
edgeCases: A workbook declaring A1:B1048576 with only 144 material contacts returns exactly 144 contacts in worker and Vercel runtimes.
CSV and XLSX with 6,001 real contacts produce the same canonical names and emails without a row-limit error.
A populated 257th column or a cell longer than 4,096 characters still fails before preview.
A forged ZIP entry larger than the expansion ceiling is rejected in local and Vercel worker modes before workbook decoding.
A third concurrent parse for one authenticated workspace receives a retryable error while two active workers complete and release their slots.
